pairs.problem: "instance-level consistency constraints" became "consistency constraints on single inputs". In Pres et al. 2026a, instance-level objectives are "symmetric consistency constraints between model input-output instances, where neither instance refers to other instances" (as opposed to meta-level objectives about the model's descriptions of its own behavior). They relate several inputs and outputs (invariance itself compares f on x and on g(x)), so "on single inputs" misstates the notion.
pairs.fix_new: [Pres et al. 2026a](./#p=pres2026consistency) place model faithfulness among instance-level consistency constraints, which relate the model's input-output pairs to one another without any of them describing the others: invariance (the output stays the same when the input is transformed), $f(g(x))=f(x)$, and equivariance (the output changes in a matching way), $f(g(x))=g'(f(x))$, for input and output transformations $g$ and $g'$.

edits.old: 231 are failure modes (named ways of being unfaithful)
edits.new: 231 are failure modes (named ways in which faithfulness or a related notion fails)
edits.problem: Added gloss is too narrow. The 231 failure-mode definitions include failures of related notions that are not unfaithfulness, e.g. 'over-promise', 'Instruction Deviation' and 'persona drift' (say-do), 'confession has honest mistake' and 'not_complied_not_reported' (honesty), 'hallucinated trigger condition' (self-report); intro.md defines the kind as 'a named way in which the notion fails'.

edits.old: 297 are criteria (conditions for a notion to apply)
edits.new: 297 are criteria (necessary or sufficient conditions for a notion, or assumptions it rests on)
edits.problem: Added gloss is imprecise. Criterion rows include necessary conditions (e.g. 'a necessary property of faithful explanation'), assumptions ('belief consistency (assumption)', 'assumption: prompts interpreted correctly') and conditions on measures, not only conditions for a notion to apply; intro.md defines the kind as 'a necessary or sufficient condition for the notion, or an assumption it rests on'.

edits.old: self-consistency (whether the model's outputs agree with each other)
edits.new: self-consistency (whether the model's outputs, such as an answer and its explanation, agree with each other or rely on the same parts of the input)
edits.problem: Added gloss covers only output-level self-consistency. Parcalabescu & Frank 2023, the main source of the term here, also define it on input contributions (CC-SHAP gauges 'how well a model's input contributions align, when it produces a prediction and explanation'), and the page later says CC-SHAP 'measures self-consistency'.

edits.old: the generated mediator (the intermediate representation the model produces)
edits.new: the generated mediator (the intermediate structure, such as a checklist or rubric, that the model writes before its decision)
edits.problem: Added gloss is misleading: in Somov et al. 2026 the mediator is an explicit written intermediate structure ('rubrics, checklists, or verification queries'), not an internal representation, which is what 'intermediate representation' suggests on a page about internal computation.
